Skink asked me to bring him a copy of Galur Rithari's papers.

Our camps have many yurts of hides stretched on chitin frames. The yurts can be quickly dismantled and packed onto the tribe's guars when moving to new grazing and hunting grounds. The khan's yurt is larger than family yurts, and surrounded by the yurts of his gulakhans.
Ashlanders think it shameful to attack unarmed persons, but we will kill without hesitation an armed person who offends us or our clan laws.
Most Ashlanders wish all foreigners and their false gods could be driven from Morrowind. At very least, we wish the foreign devils would leave us in peace.
It is safe to walk around our camp, but if your speech is offensive, we will not hesitate to challenge you.

Except for the settled southwest and the fertile Grazelands of the northeast, Vvardenfell is mostly covered by hostile desert wastes, arid grasslands, and volcanic badlands, with a few small Ashlander camps here and there.

Volume two tells of Galur Rithari, a Buoyant Armiger from Bal Ur who claimed to have been cured of vampirism. 
I have heard of another book, a set of manuscripts written by Rithari, that could be of further use to you. I had planned on asking you to recover these manuscripts once you had completed more duties, but I do not know how likely that is now, given your condition. I hope that if you find Galur Rithari's Papers, they aid you in finding a cure.
We have many books in the Hall of Justice, but our library is closed to foreigners.
You might find a copy at Jobasha's Rare Books in Vivec. He often stocks tomes others would consider... risky.

All the lands rise up to meet Red Mountain. The House Dunmer and the Imperials, they live mostly on the coasts and in the green places. The tribes hunt and herd in the Ashlands and the Grazelands. The lands across the Inner Sea are also Morrowind, but they have been claimed by the settled peoples, and I know of no Ashlanders who live there.
Yes, I would be most interested in a copy of this book. As I'm sure would you. Ask booksellers and scholars. Someone surely knows where a copy is.

These papers allegedly describe how an Ordinator from Bal Ur became a vampire and was cured. I would be most interested in a copy of this book. As, I'm sure, would you. Ask booksellers and scholars. Someone surely knows where a copy is.

Thongar the Nord runs this place, see him for supplies and sundries. If you want to get out of Khuul, S'virr and Talmeni Drethan take passengers by ship, and Seldus Nerendus is our caravaner up at the strider port.

"District" - this is an Imperial term, used by the invaders to divide. Vvardenfell is this island, from the Sea of Ghosts in the north to the Inner Sea in the south, and from the western Bitter Coast to the mushroom cities of the sorcerers in the east in the Zafirbel Bay.

They don't call it that for nothing. It's not the easiest thing to pronounce, but having it is worse. It makes your skin turn wrong, like you're covered in scales like a slaughterfish, and then it starts itching and doesn't let up. And just when you think that's as bad as it's going to get, that's when you start seeing things that aren't there. I don't know what causes it.

They don't call it that for nothing. It's not the easiest thing to pronounce, but having it is worse. It makes your skin turn wrong, like you're covered in scales like a slaughterfish, and then it starts itching and doesn't let up. And just when you think that's as bad as it's going to get, that's when you start seeing things that aren't there, or start hearing people speak when they're not even in the room. I don't know what causes it. Seems like some sort of soul sickness, if you ask me.
Serpiginous dementia is a serious common disease affecting the victim's mind and behavior. Symptoms include hallucinations and an itchy and unsightly scaly skin condition resembling snake scales.

In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derives from 'the Dark Elven Curse', which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the ash wastes, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in the Dunmer's own accounts of their past.

In Imperial stories, the dark skin and red eyes of the Dunmer derive from 'the Dark Elven Curse', which was caused by a moral taint, a sorcerous curse, and the pernicious environment of the ash wastes, according to various legends and fables. These stories may be plausibly ascribed to western Imperial racial prejudice and fear of the Dark Elves; such legends play no part in any of our own accounts of our past.

You are courteous, %PCName, so I think I will help you with this foreign prophecy. These 'silent caverns' ... Perhaps it means the ancient stronghold we call Berandas. Beneath its ruins are great caverns. Travel to the village of Gnisis, then look south, near the cave they have dedicated to their false gods. There you will find Berandas.
This is an artifact made by the gods of the foreign devils. Why should I help you find it?

The blight storms have come with fury this year. Never have I seen them so fierce. They bring new sicknesses our wise women do not know how to cure, and turn the land and the beasts against us. These are hard times for the tribes.
Stoneflower petals are collected from a small blue flower native to most parts of Vvardenfell. They are especially common in the West Gash and Azura’s Coast regions.

Stoneflower petals are collected from a small blue flower native to most parts of Vvardenfell. They are most common in the West Gash, but they can sometimes be found almost anywhere except the inland ash wastes.

Vvardenfell has nine regions. We call them the Ascadian Isles, the Ashlands, Azura's Coast, the Bitter Coast, the Grazelands, Molag Amur, Red Mountain, the West Gash, and Sheogorad. Once we grazed our herds freely, but the settled peoples and the Imperial devils have stolen all but the Ashlands and the Grazelands from us.

Be particularly careful when entering the yurts of ashkhans -- tribal chiefs -- and wise women -- our tribal seers and counselors. Some are welcoming, some are hostile. Be courteous, and leave if requested. If offended, they may attack. It is their right.
We may challenge a stranger who enters a yurt without invitation. Customs differ with different tribes, but leave when requested, and you may be forgiven.
The Urshilaku will never meet with this sorcerer. You may be Nerevarine, but your judgement is clouded by your Outlander past, or you would not ask such questions.
Know the customs of Ashlander gifts; we are not offended by gifts of money, and take them as tokens of deference and respect from the giver.

Among clan and kin, Ashlander courtesy is very proper and polite, and you are %PCRank. Few will seek to harm you. But there is still much you do not know of us. Tread carefully, and speak your words with respect.

Take care when visiting an Ashlander camp. Among clan and kin, Ashlander courtesy is very proper and polite, but you are a stranger, so remember that we have many reasons to hate foreigners, and few reasons to trust your intentions. Tread carefully, and speak your words with respect.
The most popular beverages are mazte, a local beer brewed from fermented saltrice, and sujamma, a potent, bitter liquor.
The most popular sources of protein are kwama eggs and the meat of the domesticated hound.
Bittergreen, a fast-growing plant if triggered by rain, is safe and nourishing when boiled, though it can be highly toxic if prepared incorrectly.
Hackle-lo, a hardy succulent edible leafy green, is a reliable year-round vegetable, eaten cooked or raw.
The staple is the saltrice grain, usually eaten as a cooked porridge mixed with scuttle, which is a cheese-like food from giant domesticated beetles.

The most popular sources of protein are kwama eggs and the meat of the domesticated hound. The most popular beverages are mazte, a local beer brewed from fermented saltrice, and sujamma, a potent, bitter liquor.

The staple is the saltrice grain, usually eaten as a cooked porridge mixed with scuttle, which is a cheese-like food from giant domesticated beetles. Hackle-lo, a hardy succulent edible leafy green, is a reliable year-round vegetable, eaten cooked or raw, and bittergreen, a fast-growing plant if triggered by rain, is safe and nourishing when boiled, though highly toxic if eaten raw.

Abelmawia is what the local Dark Elves call a 'hetman'. He's a kind of spokesperson for the villagers. If they have any issues, they tend to take it to him first, and he'll come complain to the Temple or the Redoran. Or me. He's got a house over by the arch.
The hetman speaks for us when we have problems, and handles affairs here for Serjo Hlaren Ramoran. If you have need of him, he keeps his hearth in his house by the arch.
He's some sort of leader for the villagers. He's got a hut just under the big arch, you can usually find him there.

This is an interesting challenge. Yes, perhaps I can help you with your Oracle's riddle. Nammu, or 'no-name', is a cavern in the wildlands of Sunna Guradan. Its east-facing entrance is west-north-west from the Daedric ruin Yansirramus. At the heart of the cavern is a great high chamber, flooded, with a central spire rising from the water. The water around the bottom of the spire might be the ring of water in darkness from the vision.
No. I will not help you find this thing of your Imperial gods. Why should I?
You should speak to Tienius Delitian about that, my friend.
Closcius? I do know the name from somewhere... Ah, yes. The proprietor of the South Wall Cornerclub, I believe. I'd avoid his establishment if you have any interest in keeping hold of your purse.
That thieving fetcher runs the South Wall Cornerclub. You'll find him there, watering down drinks and loafing about with his Thieves Guild cronies.
How should I know anything about that filthy n'wah? And if I did, why would I tell YOU?
Bacola Closcius is owner of South Wall Cornerclub.
Owns the South Wall Cornerclub, I think. Check there, he's usually about.
Among the tribes, and particularly among the Urshilaku, there is a cult that believes that the ancient hero Nerevar will be reborn to cast down the Temple and drive the Imperials out of Morrowind.

All blight diseases are to be feared, but corprus most of all. Corprus is a rare form of blight disease. Sometimes crusaders get it from fighting corprus monsters inside the Ghostfence. Not even Master Yakin Bael can cure it. Victims are sent to the Corprusarium beneath Tel Fyr, the tower of the Telvanni wizard Divayth Fyr, where they go mad, and their bodies become fat and distorted with unnatural growths. It is always fatal. Sometimes it progresses slowly, sometimes in a matter of days.

All blight diseases are to be feared, but corprus most of all.  Corprus is a rare form of blight disease. Sometimes crusaders get it from fighting corprus monsters inside the Ghostfence. We can't cure it. Victims are sent to the Corprusarium beneath Tel Fyr, the tower of the Telvanni wizard Divayth Fyr. Victims go mad, and the body becomes fat and distorted with unnatural growths. It is always fatal. Sometimes it progresses slowly, sometimes in a matter of days.
You get blight diseases by fighting with beasts carrying the sickness. There is a bad magic in the storms now. Normal creatures get caught in blight storms, go mad, turn into ugly monsters.

You're in Thongar's Tradehouse. The rest of town is just fisherman's shacks. Look around if you like. Doubt if anyone'll care. The fishing village of Ald Velothi is west along the coast, past the ruins of Ashalmawia. The silt strider goes to Ald'ruhn, Maar Gan, and Gnisis. If you're on foot, Gnisis is way south of Ald Velothi, and Maar Gan is way southeast of Khuul, and there're no good route to either.

The Temple, and Lord Vivec's holy Ash Mask, are just across the street, in the very heart of Gnisis. Koal Cave lies south, across the Ouada Samsi. For the eggmine, you'll want to turn left and head up the hill, right to the top. The Imperial Legion has claimed some of the buildings on the other side of the village. Punibi Yahaz is our caravaner - head right and look for the cargo overhang. What else? Oh. Arvs-Drelen. That's the old Velothi tower. You're Telvanni. Perhaps it's safe for you to go in there.

The Temple, and Lord Vivec's holy Ash Mask, are just across the street, in the very heart of Gnisis. Koal Cave lies south, across the Ouada Samsi. For the eggmine, you'll want to turn left and head up the hill, right to the top. The Imperial Legion has claimed some of the buildings on the other side of the village. Punibi Yahaz is our caravaner - head right and look for the cargo overhang. What else? Oh. Arvs-Drelen. That's the old Velothi tower. A Telvanni sorceror lives there. Stay away, is my advice.

The East Empire Company has offices, warehouses, and docks east of the castle, and connects to the castle by a bridge. The great statue of the Imperial dragon in the East Empire Company plaza is a visible reminder of the Empire's power and wealth here in Morrowind. Hmm... What else? You're standing in the only tavern in town. Nevosi Hlan offers ship passage to Vivec, Sadrith Mora, Hla Oad, and Tel Branora from the docks east of the dragon statue.
My Lord was most generous, but you still have the stench of the grave on you. Enjoy what is left of your life.

Galur Rithari's papers tell the story of how he was cured of the disease. According to the book, he petitioned Molag Bal for a cure at Bal Ur. Bal Ur is a shrine to Molag Bal situated to the north of Suran.
Councilor Curio is in residence at the moment.
If you wish to speak with Councilor Crassius Curio, you had best improve your manners, %PCRace. Unless you want to make him your enemy?
The great Telvanni wizards like Master Aryon make their homes in vast mushroom towers, grown by some strange sorcery. But I think most do not build forts like the Imperial devils around their towers.

The Telvanni are wicked, capricious sorcerers. They make their homes in vast, unnatural mushroom towers fueled by some dark magic we do not know of. Their servants and slaves they keep in smaller mushrooms nearby.

Delivery for him, eh? Old Caius rents a little bed-and-basket just up the hill on the north edge of town. Go out the front door -- NOT the upper door to the terrace -- then right up the stairs, then left at the top of the stairs and down to the end of the street.
What? Do I look like his mother? I might know, yes. I might tell my pals, yes. But you are not my pal.
The old fellow in trouble again, eh? He has a number of bad habits -- like forgetting to pay the Man in a timely manner. I don't know where he is. But someone around here probably does.
%Name is not sure. %PCRace should ask Bacola Closcius.
In ashlands, bad magic in dust. Bring sickness, bad dreams. No sleep. All time tired. Some time crazy, angry. Here, no.

That is the name given to those who seek to end the institution of slavery. I cannot fault their compassion, but as Duke I must contend with more than philosophical questions of right and wrong. There are practicalities - realities - that cannot be ignored.
Thieves and vandals. Petty criminal scum, in other words, who prey on the sympathies of the naive to fund their campaign to destroy our most cherished traditions.
Abolitionists are those who don't think that tradition and profit are good enough reasons to justify the misery and suffering of thousands of thinking, feeling people.

It's the law of Morrowind. Slavery is legal. The Empire doesn't like it, but the Emperor signed the Armistice, and that made it legal for us to retain our ancient laws and customs. What these abolitionists are promoting is theft of our legally held property.

It's the law of Morrowind. Slavery is legal. The Empire doesn't like it, but the Emperor signed the Armistice, and that made it legal for the Dunmer to retain their ancient laws and customs. The way I see it is, I've no chance of changing it. So if it's going to happen anyway, I'd be stupid to turn down an opportunity just because they do things differently here.

It's the law of Morrowind. Slavery is legal. The Empire doesn't like it, but Empire can go jump as far as I'm concerned. What these abolitionist fetchers are promoting is theft of the boss's legally held property, and we deal harshly with thieving n'wah around here.

It's the law of Morrowind. Slavery is legal. The Empire doesn't like it, but the Emperor signed the Armistice, and that made it legal for the Dunmer to retain their ancient laws and customs. What these abolitionists are promoting is theft of the boss's legally held property. And the boss isn't too happy about that, let me tell you.
It's the law of Morrowind. Slavery is legal. The Empire doesn't like it, but the Emperor signed the Armistice, and that made it legal for us to retain our ancient laws and customs.
Thieving n'wah scum, the lot of 'em. They'll get what's coming, you mark my words, outlander.
Sharmat send storms to ashlands, bad magic. Dust in every place. People, guar, kwama, all crazy, all bite and fight. Hard times for ashlanders. Here, not so hard.

Kogoruhn used to lie north of the magic wall around Red Mountain. It was northeast of Maar Gan and lay close to the stronghold of Falasmaryon, which I can mark on your map. Perhaps you can find your way there from the foyada Bani-Dad, but you should take care. It is a very bad place.

When you do not know the path, it is wise to seek counsel from those who have gone before. The ancestors and elders, or those who have long training in their craft, all these may guide you, if you are not too proud to ask.

It is a foolish herder who must beat his guar to control them. Nix-hounds can be tamed or drawn off with bribes of meat. But alit and kagouti you must run from, or bring the tribe's hunters to fight them. And people, they are not so different to beasts, I think. It is dangerous to mistake a kagouti for a guar.
You actually dealt with that scum in Addamasartus? Well. I am pleasantly surprised, %PCName. Thank you. I'll be sure to tell the others about this.

You wouldn't think so, but there are number of old abandoned tombs in the area. I thought this area had never been settled, but apparently, long before the Empire opened Vvardenfell up for settlement, someone put a lot of ancestors to rest here. Most of us can't get past a superstitious distaste for rooting around in ancestral tombs. But you're an outlander. It shouldn't bother you, should it?

If you are looking for work, and have skill and experience in the arcane arts, you can't do better than here at the Ald'ruhn Mages Guild. Edwinna Elbert, the guild steward, is in her own world, but she's good-hearted and sensible, if you can get her attention. And you can't advance very far in other factions around here unless you have good fighter's skills. Except the Temple, if that's to your taste. People with arcane skills can rise pretty fast in their ranks.

Ald'ruhn is fortunate in having two enchanters and two alchemists. Even though Cienne Sintieve and Llether Vari are up in the more expensive Manor District, I think you'll find the selection and service with Tanar Llervi and Anareren at the Mages Guild every bit as good. Of course, since you're part of the Mages Guild, you'll want to try Tanar Llervi and Anareren first. We get discounts.
The Sea of Ghosts is the name of the northern salt waters.

It is a poor merchant who boasts away all his secrets, but I think I may trust the Nerevarine. And perhaps you may be of aid to those of whom I speak, one day. Know this: we have dared what the House Dunmer have not, and ventured into places across the Ghostfence that they have abandoned in fear. And our boldness will make us rich. There is much ebony for the taking there.

This is a dangerous place, so none of the House people will come here. So we have kept the secret of the ebony all to ourselves. Now you know our secret, Nerevarine. You are welcome to rest here, but the ebony belongs to the tribe.

Why is the Temple so upset about this talk about the Nerevarine prophecy? Crazy old gentlemen, wandering around the ashlands and staring at the sun, talking to themselves. Big deal. 'Lord Nerevar is coming back to save Morrowind.' About time, I say. Where was he when the Empire walked in here and took over?
Why is the Temple so upset about this Nerevarine prophecy? Crazy old gentlemen, wandering around the ashlands and staring at the sun, talking to themselves. No big deal.

Optio Bologra is my Camp Prefect. He handles a lot of the day to day logistical issues we face. A damn fine officer. His background's a bit unorthodox - he doesn't have the education we normally like our officers to have - but I'm glad to have him. He gets things done.

Optio Bologra is the Camp Prefect here. He's one of us. Doesn't mean he'll go easy on you, though. He makes sure anyone causing trouble gets a bashing. So don't cause trouble, unless you want to get to know him real well.
Optio Bologra is the Camp Prefect here. He's tough, and he makes sure anyone causing trouble gets what's coming to them. So don't cause trouble, unless you want to get to know him real well.
Optio Bologra's the Camp Prefect for the Deathshead Legion. A great warrior. Even the Dark Elves and Imperials respect him.
Foyada Mamaea is a valley made by lava. It runs from the top of Red Mountain southwest through the Ghostgate to its end near the city of the Hlaalu called Balmora.
I've never heard of such a weapon. Perhaps you should consult with a savant of the settled peoples about such things.

Our mission in Morrowind is not an easy one. It takes a strong will and personality to thrive among people who are often indifferent or outright hostile to the Nine. Our day to day work involves curing the sick with spells of healing, divination, and persuading others to support our cause here. While we eschew senseless violence and prefer to go about our work unarmored, it is sometimes necessary to defend ourselves with blunt weapons or by conjuring magical aid.

House Telvanni seeks candidates of high intelligence and dominant will, who understand that true power comes from the application of those virtues. We generally prize all the arts of spellcasting and enchantment, although most Telvanni find that they have little use for the schools of Restoration and Alchemy. We do not expect our retainers to minister to the sick as if they were priests.

These growths and sores, this is the Curse-of-Flesh. Corprus disease. If you are the Nerevarine, you will find a way to break this curse to pass the Second Trial. Or perhaps you are not the Nerevarine, and you should make your goodbyes before the curse steals your mind as well as your flesh.

The two most common herd animals of the Ashlanders are the guar and the shalk. The guar is a large biped, trained as a beast of burden, and raised for meat and hides. Wild guars are commonly encountered in the wilderness, too. The shalk is a large beetle, raised for meat and resin from its shells.
Black anther is a flowering plant that grows in the Ascadian Isles and less commonly along Azura's Coast.
Black anther is a flowering plant native to Vvardenfell. It grows in the Ascadian Isles and along Azura's Coast.
A lot of diseases will make your muscles twitch and spasm, but you'll always know it's rust chancre if you've got it, because it also makes you break out in a great ugly rash all over.
Rust chancre is a mild common disease affecting a victim's mobility and appearance. Symptoms include swelling and rash, and painful muscle spasms.

Sometimes the shalk have a sickness on them, and when they pass it to us, we call it Collywobbles. It is a serious thing. It makes you shake out of all control, so that no energy is left for anything else.

Collywobbles is a disease sometimes carried by shalk beetles. It's easy to identify, because victims can't stop shaking and twitching. They shake so long and so hard that it wears them down, and they have no energy left for anything else. In the very worst cases, they don't even have the strength to eat or drink, and they waste away.
One of the local Dark Elves. Heard she lost her husband in the eggmine. Must be hard for her.

You're a friend, but I admit I'm troubled by what you've done. That family already lost husband and father, but to have their ancestral land stolen from under them too? Aiee. It is a bad thing, %PCName, and I don't know if it is possible to make amends for it.
Widow Vabdas told us what you did, honourless Imperial dog. You shame your ancestors.
He died while he was out on a hunting trip.
Here, yes. Drinking, yes.

Kresh fiber is a resinous fiber with modest magical properties that comes from the coarse grass called kreshweed. It grows well near salt water, particularly Azura's Coast and West Gash regions, but also along the coasts of Sheogorad region.
Kresh fiber is a resinous fiber with modest magical properties that comes from the coarse grass of the West Gash and Azura's Coast called kreshweed. It can also be found in Sheogorad region.
Mudcrab bites sometimes pass a sickness that makes sensible hunters babble like the Mad One has touched them. This we call Swamp Fever.
Swamp fever sounds scarier than it is. It makes people talk nonsense, but if you put them to bed and let them sweat it out they mostly recover just fine.

Swamp fever hits hard, makes you babble until your temperature comes down again, but it's not really serious. Most people recover quickly. You can catch swamp fever anywhere there are mudcrabs, but it's worst in the Bitter Coast. I hear Seyda Neen is riddled with it.

Swamp fever is a mild common disease affecting the victim's strength and behavior. You find it all over the Empire, anywhere you find mudcrabs really. Symptoms include high body temperature and delirium.
Sometimes when hunters get in a tangle with kagouti, they come back with dark, bruise-like swelling, sensitive to the touch, even though they weren't wounded. That is the disease Yellow Tick.
Yellow tick makes you break out in dark, bruise-like swellings that are sensitive to touch. Wise travelers avoid kagouti anyway, but yellow tick's another reason not to get too close.

Yellow tick is a mild common disease affecting a victim's strength and mobility. Symptoms include dark, bruise-like swelling, sensitive to touch. It may be contracted from the kagouti, or from plague wolves.
Ash-chancre is a blight disease that makes its victims repulsive. It comes of contact with corprus beasts or other blight monsters.
Black-heart blight robs its victims of their strength and endurance. It is carried by corprus beasts and other blight monsters.
Except for the southwest where the big cities of the settled people lie, Vvardenfell is covered by hostile desert wastes, arid grasslands, and volcanic badlands.

Except for the settled southwest and the fertile Grazelands of the northeast, Vvardenfell is mostly covered by hostile desert wastes, arid grasslands, and volcanic badlands, and thinly populated by the nomadic Ashlander tribes.

The foreign devils weren't always here. It is only in recent seasons that they have swarmed the island. Before, it was only the tribes, and a few cities of the settled Dunmer -- their holy city of Vivec and the old Great House cities of Balmora, Ald'ruhn, and Sadrith Mora.
Vvardenfell was an old name for Red Mountain, before the Inner Sea was made. Now we call the island Vvardenfell.
Our legends say that in Nerevar's time, there was no inner sea to separate.

It's hard to miss. Everything else here is made out of bug shell, or at least looks that way. Not very big, much like the Deathshead Legion itself. It's a relatively young Legion posted here, with a lot of new recruits. Not much fighting, not very prestigious. A lot of my job is keeping them disciplined and busy enough not to go MAKING fights.
There, see? Nelos.
Thank you for rescuing me from that place.
Bolvyn Venim had me secretly arrested and is holding me hostage here.
Venim Manor? The entrance is in the southeast corner.
I am King Helseth's personal champion. Like the rest of his Royal Guard, I protect my liege and do battle on his behalf.
Dead thing! No! Get away!
We have reached an agreement already, vampire. Leave me.
I have little interest in speaking with you, vampire. Get on with it and begone.
A vampire. How... irregular. Well, I assume you're here for a reason. What is it?
Back again, vampire? What is it you want?
A vampire. Here, talking. How intriguing. What is it you want, vampire?
A vampire. Interesting. Not many of your kind dare show their face among the living. What brings you here?
Vampire! I curse you, in the name of all the ancestors. Return to the foul corruption from which you came! Die, fiend!
Vampire! Accursed fiend! I will strike you down, in the name of Lord Dagoth!
Vampire! Accursed fiend! I will strike you down, in the name of the ancestors!
Vampire! You defile this holy place with your presence. I curse you, in the name of all the ancestors. Return to the foul corruption from which you came! Die, fiend!

Well, well. A vampire. In Morrowind. And still alive... so to speak. [Chuckles.] What brings you to me? If you're looking for a vampirism cure, I can't help you. But I can tell you where to start looking. Or do you simply seek to talk?
Remarkable. A vampire. In Morrowind. And still alive... so to speak. [Chuckles.] If you're looking for a vampirism cure, I can't help you. But perhaps I can tell you where to start looking.
Wear clothes, %PCName.
You bear corprus-curse. Leave! Away!
You bear the corprus curse. I do not know what this means. Perhaps it is a sign of the Second Trial. Perhaps it means nothing.
You breathed bad magic in dust, fell blight-sick. Need healers, potions, not talk. Go now.
You have slain one of my tribe. Their spirit demands retribution.
So. The Sharmat is dead by your hand, Nerevarine. Our sleep is easy now. You are thrice-welcome in these caverns and at our hearths; we have much to thank you for.

Ai. Our Ashkhan has named you Nerevarine. It is a strange thing, to think that an outlander may be Nerevarine, but if our Ashkhan and Wise Woman are convinced, it is not for me to doubt. We will not harm you, if you need to rest here from your trials, %PCRank.
We heard the Urshilaku named an outlander %PCRank. We wish no fight with the Urshilaku, but this is a Zainab place. It is not for you, %PCRank. You should leave.
What are you doing here, Hlaalu? With what treachery have you found this place? Leave. Now. We have made agreements with your House, but this is our ebony.
Leave, outlander. This place is not for you.
You have a sickness, %PCName. Common, no danger. But find healer, yes?
People say %PCName dangerous. Big outlaw. Break many laws.
All quiet here, %PCRank. More's the pity. Could do with a bit of action.
Could be worse, I suppose. At least it's not Solstheim, eh %PCRank?
How can I help, %PCRank?
Any news, %PCRank?
What new grief do you bring my family this time, %PCRace? Speak, if you must, but know this: I can do nothing to retaliate, but the ancestors spit on you.
You've a lot of nerve showing your face around here after what you did to Widow Vabdas, %PCRace. I hope you're ashamed of yourself.
When you're in Gnisis, do me a favor. Don't talk to me. I don't like you, and it just ruins my day to have to put up with someone I don't like.
South Wall is cornerclub owned by Bacola Closcius, near south wall of city on east side of river. Many of %Name's friends go there.
That's where the Thieves Guild scum hang out. So why are you me asking about it?
That's on Labor Street, east side of the Odai. Near the south wall. Obviously.

We hunt, herd guar. Honor ancestors. Move always. No house, only yurt. Me, I herd guar. Then blight storms and soul sickness come. Now, no guar. I come here. Work, fight, make gold. Become rich like great trader.
We are the Ashlanders, the true followers of Veloth. We honor and worship our ancestors. Our tribes are led by our ashkhan war chiefs, and guided by the wisdom and prophecies of our wise women.
By tradition, we have the right to raid the settled people and other Ashlander tribes for treasures and slaves.
We are the People of the Wastes. Our camps and yurts move with the herds, and we hunt wildlife for meat and hides.
There are rumors... I can't be sure. But I've heard they help slaves escape and return to their homes, or to make new lives in safe places.

Greenspore makes calm, level-headed people angry at everything, and prone to shouting and violent outbursts. It clouds the mind, too, makes you hear and see things that aren't there. Sometimes its victims are never quite the same, even after they're cured.
Greenspore is a serious common disease affecting a victim's behavior. Symptoms include irritability and violent outbursts, and may include mild dementia.

Greenspore is a serious common disease affecting a victim's behavior common throughout the Empire wherever slaughterfish are found, although I've noticed that fewer slaughterfish here seem to carry it than in Cyrodiil. Symptoms include irritability and violent outbursts, and may include mild dementia.

The regular rain and dark soils of the Grazelands produce the rich grazing for Ashlander herds that gives the region its name. The region lies in the northeast of Vvardenfell, sandwiched between the Ashlands and Azura's Coast. Permanent settlements include Vos village and the Telvanni tower of Tel Vos. The Ashlanders of Zainab camp move their herds across the plains in search of fresh grazing. There are no paved roads, but travel is easy across the open plains.

The regular rain and dark soils of the Grazelands produce the rich grazing for Ashlander herds that gives the region its name. The region lies in the northeast of Vvardenfell, sandwiched between the Ashlands and Azura's Coast. Permanent settlements include Vos village and the towers of Tel Vos. The Ashlanders of Zainab camp move their herds across the plains in search of fresh grazing. There are no paved roads, but travel is easy across the open plains.
There are no paved roads in the Grazelands, but travel is easy across the rolling plains.
A herd cannot stay in the same place forever. We Ashlanders of Zainab camp move our herds across the Grazelands in search of fresh fodder.
The only permanent settlements in the Grazelands are Vos village and the wizard's tower of Tel Vos.
Permanent settlements in the Grazelands include Vos village and the tower of Tel Vos.
The regular rain and dark soils of the Grazelands make the rich green grass that feeds our herds.

The piercing light of the Grand Pharos at the mouth of the harbor of the port village of Seyda Neen is a beacon to mariners throughout the Inner Sea. Most visitors from the Empire make landfall at the port of Seyda Neen, where they are processed by the Imperial Census and Excise Commission agents of the Coastguard station. The Coastguard cutters docked there control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.
The Coastguard cutters of the Census and Excise Commission usually dock at Seyda Neen. Their job is to control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.
The Coastguard cutters of the Census and Excise Commission docked here help control smuggling and piracy on the Inner Sea.
My name is %Name. I am the keeper in charge of this lighthouse, which we call the Grand Pharos.
They are a group that reveres Tiber Septim.

Dagoth Ur is also called the Devil or the Sharmat. He is our ancient enemy. He sends bad dreams and blighted monstrosities to test our faith and tempt the weak, but under the protection of the Tribunal, the ancestors, and the saints we stand strong against him. He cannot cross the Ghostfence, and our brave warriors at Ghostgate repulse any incursions by his foul minions.

It's Dagoth Ur who poisons us with soul sickness and sends our neighbours screaming mad in the night. I used to think it didn't happen to good Temple-fearing Dunmer. Lately I'm not so sure. But don't spread that about, alright? I don't want anyone thinking I'M having bad dreams.
Three save us, why do you want to talk about that? Dagoth Ur is the Devil and the Enemy, and that's all I need to know.

Dagoth Ur is the ancient enemy of the blessed Three. He sleeps beneath Red Mountain, foul and evil, and sends his deformed monsters and bad dreams to test our faith. The Tribunal and our honored ancestors maintain the great Ghostfence to keep us safe.

Morrowind is the ancient homeland of the Dunmer people. Once, long ago, this was our land, but now the creatures from the West have come, and the House Dunmer have meekly submitted to their rule. Now, in all Morrowind, only the Ashlanders still lead the free, reverent lives of honor of the ancient Dunmer.
I've never treated a case of Rockjoint, but I hear it's worse than the disease the racers carry, which we call Helljoint. It makes your joints swell up and get stuck.
Rockjoint's rare, thankfully. It's a nasty one. It's like Helljoint, except instead of making everything stiff and a bit sore, it locks up your joints entirely, to the point that you can barely move.
Rockjoint is an acute common disease affecting a victim's manual dexterity. Symptoms include painful swelling and immobility of all joints.
The racers carry Helljoint sometimes. Your joints become sore and swollen, and it's hard to do fine work.

No-one needs an excuse to avoid cliff-racers, but Helljoint would be a good one if you did. It's not serious, really, but it's not pleasant either. It makes all your joints inflamed and sore, and makes it hard to do anything with any sort of finesse. And of course it always comes on when you're miles away from home. When else?

Brown rot causes the flesh to turn bad and stinking, and keeps you awake with the pain no matter how tired you get. I don't see it very often. My people know better than to disturb the dead in their tombs.

Brown rot? It's where the flesh around a wound goes rotten and stinking, and supposedly it's so painful that you can't sleep. I wouldn't worry about it. You only catch brown rot from bonewalkers, and most travelers will never encounter one, unless it's one of their own ancestral guardians. Only grave robbers get brown rot.

Brown rot is a mild common disease affecting the victim's strength and behavior. Symptoms include local necrosis around wounds and acute sleeplessness. It may be contracted from the bonewalkers that guard our ancestral tombs. Healers swear oaths to help others, of course, but I've known more than one healer refuse to treat a case of brown rot. It's unpleasant to deal with, and more often than not it was contracted in the course of grave robbery. Outlanders, mostly, of course.

Brown rot is a mild common disease affecting the victim's strength and behavior. It may be contracted from the undead constructs called bonewalkers. Symptoms include sleeplessness and necrosis around any wounds inflicted by the bonewalker.
Sometimes the blight monsters carry a disease called chanthrax. It makes its victims horribly clumsy and slow.

I've heard some say that vampirism is a disease. But no wise woman has ever been able to cure it, and I've never heard of a sorcerer's spell that could cure it either. But I admit, I've never encountered a vampire, and never thought about how to cure one. We would destroy them on sight if we could.
All I know is that Nords live there. We drove the Nords out of Morrowind once, but we know they are always scheming to return and steal our lands. Perhaps Dagon Fel is where they scheme now.
Sheogorad is largely hostile and uninhabited, except for the fishers at Ald Redaynia and the Nords who scheme in the shadows at the great ruins at Dagon Fel.
The Lady Barenziah is my liege's mother. She was Queen in Wayrest when I first entered King Helseth's service.
Bonemeal is a finely ground powder with modest magical properties made from the bones of the bonewalker, skeleton, bonelord and other animated bone-constructs of both profane and sacred origins.

We might be outcast, but I am a wise woman. I am councilor to my tribe, small as it is. I am the guardian of secret knowledge, spirit guide and seer into the world unseen. I can tell you about the ancestors, and about Ashlander customs. I know much. But there is much I have yet to learn. To my shame, I am not skilled in healing arts.
I oversee House Hlaalu's administrative affairs here in Caldera.

The lighthouse guards this part of the coast. My duty is to light the fires at dusk or in bad weather, and ensure that they stay lit until visibility is good again. If I fail in that, passing ships could easily run aground in the darkness. It is a grave responsibility.

I look after the spiritual needs of my flock of head-smashers. It's hard to get them to sit and listen to sermons, but you can get a lot done by listening to them instead. They're bored, and far from home. I've always got visitors down here. The Dark Elves aren't interested in anything I have to tell them, of course. Lost cause there.

I am a commoner. I do whatever needs doing -- cooking, cleaning, building, baking, making, breaking. And I can tell YOU'RE an outlander. Since you're new to these parts, perhaps you'd like me to share a little local lore.

I am a nightblade. Blending the disciplines of the agent and wizard, I move unseen and undetected, foil locks and traps, and teleport to safety when threatened, or strike like a viper from ambush. The College of Illusion hides me and fuddles or pacifies my opponents. The College of Mysticism detects my object, reflects and dispels enemy spells, and makes good my escape. For the right price, I'll sell you some of those spells.

I am a Battlemage. Though arrayed as a Western knight with heavy armor, axes and long blades, my primary training is in the College of Alteration, the College of Destruction, and the College of Conjuration. To round out my education, I have mastered enchantments and alchemy. To round out my income, I sell spells.

I am a healer. I have sworn solemn oaths in the College of Restoration to heal the afflicted and cure the diseased. But I have also studied both the unarmed, unarmored martial arts of the Khajiit and the light armored and blunt weapon styles of the Imperial West, both for self-defense, and for disabling or killing dangerous opponents. I sell spells, and I am a spellmaker who creates spells to your specifications. I also sell healing potions and ingredients.

I am a mage. My study is the destruction and alteration of the visible and invisible world. I study magic for its pure intellectual challenge and rewards, but I am paid in gold for the practical applications of my knowledge. I defend myself with spells of the College of Destruction, and leap, swim, and levitate with the spells of the College of Alteration. I sell spells, and I am a spellmaker who creates spells to your specifications.
I am a monk. Here at Holamayan, away from most ordinary cares of the world, most of my time is given over to prayer, and contemplation of the deeper mysteries of our texts and faith.

I am a monk. In mind and spirit, I am a student of the hidden mysteries, of the unseen world that lies behind the objects and ideas of everyday life. In body, I am a student of the ancient martial arts. I pursue hand-to-hand and unarmored self-defense, because what you don't have, you cannot lose. I also train with the blunt weapons called staves, because even the poorest peasant can own a staff. To earn my keep, I train others in my skills.

I am a monk. In mind and spirit, I am a student of the hidden mysteries, of the unseen world that lies behind the objects and ideas of everyday life. In body, I am a student of the ancient martial arts. I pursue hand-to-hand and unarmored self-defense, because what you don't have, you cannot lose. I also train with the blunt weapons called staves, because even the poorest peasant can own a staff.
I guess you could say that I live by my wits. I know how to stay one jump ahead. And for the right price, I can teach others the tools and tricks of the trade as well.
Oh, I do a little of this, a little of that. Whatever it takes to make a living, you know?

I'm a scout. I know places, people, plants, paths, wind, and weather. I serve as guide for the tribe, and bring news of trouble ahead, so that we may go around it or fight fiercely. I know the geography of Morrowind, and how to survive in the various geographic regions. My best defense is stealth, sneaking past trouble, but I can fight bow or blade if I must fight.
Dampworm is a nasty common disease that makes it difficult to move properly. It makes your muscles twitch and spasm.
Dampworm is a serious common disease affecting a victim's mobility. Symptoms include uncontrollable muscle spasms and twitching.

The settled Dunmer have a village called Maar Gan just south of the Foyada Bani-Dad, and a great city of crabshells called Ald'ruhn further south. The foreign devils have a fortress called Buckmoth there.
The Ashlands are home to the Urshilaku. Between the Sea of Ghosts and the great Ghostfence of the false gods that holds back the blight beasts, none can match us.
The Ashlands are dry wastelands around Red Mountain, home to our tribe.

Vampires are monsters that feed on blood. Once they were mortal like you and me, but they get the blood disease from another vampire, and they become vampires themselves. That's why they still exist. Everyone hates them, yet no one wants to come near one. But doesn't prophecy say the Nerevarine has nothing to fear from disease? So you have nothing to worry about, I'm sure.

Vampires are monsters that hide in the lifeless ruins of the Dwemer and the tombs of the settled people. Here in the camp we are safe from such abominations, but sometimes outcasts and foolish youngsters take risks that wiser hunters would not. We have lost more than one headstrong young hunter who thought to destroy the beasts that live in Druscashti.

Vampires are monsters that hide in the lifeless ruins of the Dwemer and the tombs of the settled people. In the camps we are safe from such abominations, but sometimes outcasts and foolish youngsters travel too close to the dark places and are lost. Ai. They are to be feared, outlander.

Vampires are monsters that feed on blood. Once they were mortal like you and me, but they get the blood disease from another vampire, and they become vampires themselves. That's why they still exist. Everyone hates them, yet no one wants to come near one.

We are the dark walkers, those who prey on the warm blooded. Our gifts are many, and weaknesses few. There are three major clans: Aundae, Berne, and Quarra. There are others in this world as well, living like cattle in tombs under the ground.

Redoran retainers and kin will find a warm welcome here. Otherwise, Saetring the Nord is an independent smith, and Vasesius Viciulus is a trader. The slave trader is Zabarbael. The Temple faithful will find a monk, healer, and apothecary at Molag Mar Temple.

The faithful will find a monk, healer, and apothecary here in the Temple. Saetring the Nord is our local independent smith, and Vasesius Viciulus is a trader. The slave trader is Zabarbael. Redoran retainers and kin have their own smith, drillmaster, trader, and savant with the Redoran garrison.

Saetring the Nord is our local independent smith, and Vasesius Viciulus is a trader. The slave trader is Zabarbael. The Temple faithful will find a monk, healer, and apothecary at Molag Mar Temple. Redoran retainers and kin have their own smith, drillmaster, trader, and savant with the Redoran garrison. Dilami Androm and Rindral Dralor can offer you transport out of Molag Mar.

I'm the publican here at the Six Fishes. We rent beds, and sell food and sundries. The Imperial cult shrine services include a priest, healer, monk, enchanter, apothecary, trader, and savant. The Imperial Legion services of the Hawkmoth Legion Garrison include a healer, smith, master-at-arms, scout, trader, chaplain, and battlemage. For other services, visit Vivec City -- the Foreign Quarter, in particular, for Fighters Guild and Mages Guild services, and the Great House compounds for kin and retainers.

I'm a trader with a fine selection of goods to choose from, just take a look around. If I don't have what you need, the ladies at the End of the World might. You're out of luck if you need a smithy or a healer, though. Dagon Fel doesn't have anyone with those skills.

If you need to pawn anything off, I'm your woman. Fryfnhild on the other side is a general trader. If we don't have what you need, I suppose you could try Heifnir, too. We don't have a smith or a healer.

I'm a trader. Take a look around, let me know if you see anything you like. Hjotra the Peacock, also here at the End of the World, is a pawnbroker; she buys and sells many things. If we don't have what you need, I suppose you could try Heifnir, too. We don't have a smith or a healer.

You'll find House Hlaalu and general administrative services here in the hall. Shenk's Shovel, the tradehouse by the South Gate, has beds, food, and sundries. Hodlismod the Nord is our smith, Verick Gemain our trader, Irgola our pawnbroker, and Falanaamo our clothier. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.

Hmm, let's see. We have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade here, and the guide network stop of course. Various other folks in town offer training. Shenk's Shovel, the tradehouse by the South Gate, has beds, food, and sundries. Verick Gemain is our trader, Hodlismod the Nord our smith, Irgola our pawnbroker, and Falanaamo our clothier. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast.

I'm Caldera's pawnbroker. Whether you need money or a great bargain, I'm your man. By the gates is Shenk's Shovel, for company, food, and beds. Otherwise, Hodlismod is our smith, Falanaamo our clothier, and Verick Gemain round the corner is our trader. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.

The name's Verick Gemain, trader. Feel free to browse. Next door is Shenk's Shovel, where you'll find beds, food, and sundries. Otherwise, Hodlismod our smith, Falanaamo our clothier, and Irgola our pawnbroker. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.

I'm Shenk, the proprietor. You'll find a clean bed and a hot meal for a fair price here. Verick Gemain is our trader, Hodlismod our smith, Falanaamo our clothier, and Irgola our pawnbroker. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.

I make and sell clothing, particularly of the traditional Western style. Shenk's Shovel, the tradehouse by the South Gate, has beds, food, and sundries. Verick Gemain is our trader, Hodlismod our smith, and Irgola our pawnbroker. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.

I'm the smith. Shenk's Shovel, the tradehouse by the South Gate, has beds, food, and sundries. Verick Gemain is our trader, Irgola our pawnbroker, and Falanaamo our clothier. House Hlaalu services are available at the big Governor's Hall on the hill to the northeast. The Mages Guild is in the southwest corner of town; they have an alchemist, enchanter, mage, and nightblade. Various other folks in town offer training.
Balmora is our district seat on Vvardenfell, but the councillors largely prefer to conduct their business elsewhere.
Balmora's not so bad. There's plenty of opportunity here, if you know the right places to look.

I don't know anything about High Town, really, but by the cut of your clothes that's where you'll want to be looking. The nobles have all their fancy manors up there, and it's got all the pricy shops too.

I don't know anything about High Town. Someone like you probably wants the Imperial Guilds along Market Street, they've got the best prices if you're lucky enough to be a member. Otherwise, someone like Ra'virr or Dralasa Nithryon probably have what you're looking for, unless you're looking for a bed. Then you want the Lucky Lockup. The South Wall'll rob you blind, the Plates will do the same with prettier words, and the folks at the Council Club'll kill you in your sleep.
You're standing in it. What more do you need to know? I suppose I could tell you more, if there's something in it for me.

Balmora's a big place, but it's easy enough to find your way around once you get used to it. High Town's up on the west hill, with all the noble's manors and the fancy shops. For more reasonable prices, or the Imperial Guilds, or a quick trip out on a strider, you want the market near the South Gate. The Temple's by the North Gate. Along the banks and over in Labor Town it's all houses, except the South Wall Cornerclub.

There is a disease you can catch from rats that turns your thoughts all wrong, makes you forget things you've known all your life, and act in ways no-one else can understand. We call this disease witbane.

Have you ever woken up in the middle of nowhere and had no idea how you got there, or how to get home, or even where home is? Might have been witbane. You catch it from rat bites, and it turns your mind all funny until you get treated. Makes it hard to remember your own name.
Rattles is a mild disease that causes muscle spasms and listlessness. Victims say they aren't tired, but they can't bring themselves to do any work.

Rattles is a bit like Dampworm. They both make your muscles spasm, but Rattles isn't as severe as Dampworm. I can tell you from experience that when you have Rattles you don't want to do anything but curl up in bed and not move for a week, though.
Rattles is a mild common disease affecting a victim's willpower and dexterity. Symptoms include muscle spasms and listlessness.
Ash-woe is a blight disease that makes its victims weak-willed and deranged. It comes from corprus beasts or other blighted creatures.

Corprus is a deadly disease that attacks a victim's mind and body. Victims grow mad and violent, and their bodies sprout wild, revolting growths. It comes from contact with corprus beasts or other blight monsters.
I have served the King since I was a child.

Skooma is a narcotic made from refined moon sugar. It makes you fast and strong, but clumsy and stupid. The trade in skooma is very lucrative, but also highly illegal, of course, which makes it difficult to buy unless you have the right connections.

We healers and wise women always worry when we hear of an outbreak of chills in a camp. It strikes fast and spreads, makes you clumsy and confused and cold even through blankets in summer. Experienced hunters lose their way, wander lost on the trails until they're found. Strong men, made weak as scribs.

Chills is extremely dangerous. It comes on fast, makes you confused and clumsy. I've had it before and let me tell you, it lives up to the name. You can be standing next to a pool of lava and still feel freezing. You need to get help as soon as possible, or you'll be easy pickings for anything that finds you out there.
Chills is an extremely dangerous common disease affecting the victim's mind and coordination. Symptoms include clumsiness and mental confusion. It's unfortunately common among pilgrims.
Chills is an extremely dangerous common disease affecting the victim's mind and coordination. Symptoms include clumsiness and mental confusion.
Yes, but I am outcast. The Wise Women will not cure me. Tunipy would cure me, but she does not know the right herbs and rituals.

Droops is carried by kwama. It makes your muscles weak and limp - that's where the name comes from. We have two kwama mines here in Vos, so I see a lot of Droops. It's a nightmare for the overseers. If the infection isn't noticed in time, all the miners can get sick at the same time, and production has to stop.

Droops is mostly a problem for kwama miners, although travelers sometimes pick it up from roaming kwama as well. The name comes from the way victims start to droop as the disease sets in - it makes your muscles limp and weak.

Droops is a serious common disease that affects a victim's strength. Symptoms include weak and flaccid muscle tissues. It may be contracted from most forms and stages of kwama. It's most common among kwama miners.
Droops is a serious common disease that affects a victim's strength. Symptoms include weak and flaccid muscle tissues. You only really hear of it here in Morrowind, because it's carried by kwama.

Ataxia is a disease spread by alits that makes you weak and clumsy. It makes your muscles stiff, and everything hurts. All Ashlanders know it well. Our hunters often catch it when they go out to protect the herds and bring back hides.

Sometimes alits carry Ataxia. It makes you weak and clumsy, your muscles all stiffen up, and everything hurts. It's not serious if you're tucked up in bed with a warm mug of shein, but it's not something you want to catch when you're out on the trail and already loaded down with gear.
Ataxia is a mild common disease affecting the victim's strength and dexterity. Symptoms include generalized pain and muscle stiffness. It may be contracted from alits.

Ataxia is a mild common disease affecting the victim's strength and dexterity. Symptoms include generalized pain and muscle stiffness. It may be contracted from alits - and bears, too, although you should be safe from those here on Vvardenfell.
Wither catches the breath, makes men gasp like slaughterfish caught on land. It doesn't kill, but it does make you very weak.
Wither makes it hard to catch your breath. And when you can't breathe, everything else feels harder. You're weak, tired, can hardly go three steps without wanting to take a break.
Wither is a mild common disease that affects a victim's strength and endurance. Symptoms include loss of energy and shortness of breath.
As I keep telling my troops, it's not the most interesting posting in Tamriel, but it's strategically important for us.

Not much happens here. Dark Elves do their thing in the mine, the General argues with their nobles and priests, pilgrims come and cry a lot over some dust at the Temple. More fighting would be better.

It's a holy site for the Dark Elves. They don't like us being here much, but they can't do much about it, and they mostly leave me alone as long as I stick to teaching outlanders. They get hostile real quick if you start talking about the Nine to natives.

Gnisis is one of Vvardenfell's most holy sites. Lord Vivec's sacred Ash Mask resides here in the Temple at the Shrine of Justice, guarded by Ordinators. To the south across the Ouada Samsi is Koal Cave, where Vivec defeated Ruddy Man, father of the dreugh, and demonstrated to all Dunmer the virtue of valor.

This is a Temple town, ruled by House Redoran. Not that you'd know it with all you Orcs stomping about. Most of us here work in the mine, or walk the trade trails along the West Gash. It's a holy place, so there are always pilgrims looking to buy supplies from our merchants.

This is a Temple town, ruled by House Redoran. Not that you'd know it with all these Orcs stomping about. Most of us here work in the mine, or walk the trade trails along the West Gash. It's a holy place, so there are always pilgrims looking to buy supplies from our merchants.

We are the devoted servants and faithful of the Tribunal. We worship and revere Almalexia the Healing Mother, Sotha Sil the Teacher, and Vivec the Warrior-Poet, who are together known as Almsivi. It is our duty and privilege to share their mercy, wisdom, and justice with the people of Morrowind, and to guide the faithful to righteous paths.
Dark Elves don't like us. S'alright, we don't like them neither. They're better than Bretons, though, I gotta give 'em that. They're tough out here.

'Foyada' means 'fire-river' in our language. The deep, ash-dark ravines which run down from the Red Mountain volcano are called foyada. The lava from Red Mountain is very fluid, and runs almost like water. During an eruption, fire-rivers run down the mountain, clearing the ravines. Because they have good footing, are clear of brush, and run long distances, we use them like roads when traveling overland.
Well hello there.
Hmm.
A nudist! How wonderful! You seem to be a lively spirit.
Khuul is just a fishing village. Not much else here. You can rent a bed here at Thongar's Tradehouse. But other than the Daedric ruins to the southwest, there's not much around here worth looking at.

We've got local fare. It's filling, and priced to move. We've got the local brews, greef, shein, mazte and sujamma. They're cheap, and full of kick. I've got the good stuff, too, behind the counter -- Cyrodiilic brandy and flin -- but it ain't cheap. And if you've got a bit of a sweet tooth, could be that we can find something to satisfy that, if the price is right.
